name: Botulinum toxin for hair loss

lead:
Botulinum toxin is the neuromodulator behind Botox, Dysport and Xeomin. Its established cosmetic role is smoothing frown lines. For hair, small intradermal scalp injections have been trialled in androgenetic alopecia, the common pattern hair loss.
The idea is that relaxing scalp muscle and reducing tension might improve blood flow and hair growth. If it worked this way it would help looks by thickening hair. This remains an investigational approach; the evidence base is small.

paras: Treatment is a clinic procedure with a licensed injector, in which tiny amounts are placed in the skin of the scalp. People often describe it as an add-on to other hair treatments. Details of products and amounts are set by clinicians.

Botulinum toxin is a prescription product. Documented cosmetic side effects include bruising, muscle weakness and, rarely, partial facial paralysis and difficulty swallowing [1]. Scalp use for hair loss is not an approved indication.

chain: Proposed to relax scalp muscle and improve blood flow
angle.text: The goal is thicker-looking hair in androgenetic alopecia. The mechanism is proposed rather than established, and use is investigational.

lead: Botulinum toxin products such as Botox Cosmetic, Dysport, Xeomin and Jeuveau are best known for temporarily reducing facial wrinkles, especially frown lines [1]. Intradermal injection into the scalp has been studied as a possible treatment for androgenetic alopecia, and the brand Xeomin is among those mentioned in discussions of "Xeomin hair".

Researchers who propose the approach suggest that scalp muscle tension compresses small vessels and that relaxing the muscle may improve circulation to follicles; this is a hypothesis described by proponents rather than an established mechanism. For appearance, the hoped-for outcome is greater hair density.
Botulinum toxin is a prescription medicine with approved cosmetic uses such as glabellar lines (Botox Cosmetic was approved in the US in 2002) [1]. Hair-loss use is investigational.

paras: Cosmetic botulinum toxin effects typically last about two to four months and usually begin within days of injection [1].
Cosmetic use is associated with bruising, muscle weakness, partial facial paralysis and swallowing difficulty in some cases [1].
Small trials of scalp injection in androgenetic alopecia have been reported in the dermatology literature.

timeline.event: Botox Cosmetic approved in the US for glabellar lines [1].
